Root cause: input routing and the frame builder derived the tile layout viewport differently. border_width_px is authored in the 2x design-pixel space; routing inset by ui_design_px(border_width_px) (metal_tile_content_viewport), matching what both backends draw and what tile_content_border_insets maps pointer coordinates through, while the frame builder (metal_tile_inner_extents, ui/frame.rs) used the raw value. Runtime::set_layout_viewport_exact compares viewports bit-exactly, so every routed input event laid the tree out for one viewport and the next frame laid it out again for the other: two full LayoutEngine passes per frame, on any buffer, no scroll widget involved. Confirmed live on the reference machine (display scale 1.6 -> ui_px_scale 0.8, show_border/border_width_px at their non-zero tile defaults). Only the wgpu shell calls set_ui_scale_factor, which is why macOS never saw it.

Root causes (measured by the new probes, debug pre-fix -> release post-fix):
1. Triton ADSR gesture start: active-adsr was a defstate read at build time by every stage-readout subtree, so the FIRST drag event of each gesture synchronously re-rendered ~25 subtrees — first-drag dispatch 1957ms (debug) -> 5.96ms (release). Now gesture-local state projected into per-stage SEQV float fields the number pickers bind (the *sel-sync* precedent); value-equal writes short-circuit mid-gesture.
2. Cold focus: the per-widget primitive cache key hashed the GLOBAL focused-widget id, invalidating every cacheable widget in the tile on any focus/tile change. Every consumer only asks 'am I focused', so the id is narrowed per node before keying/building.
3. Per-event global widget-state-generation bumps from widget-local interaction state (adsr envelope, knob-number/number-picker edit state, response-curve live band) defeated every widget's primitive cache each drag frame on the always-dynamic wgpu path. Those sites now bump a per-widget revision hashed into the owning widget's key; widget_state_generation() still advances on every bump so redraw scheduling and metal tile-scene fingerprints observe changes (macOS behavior preserved by construction; not run on a Mac — eseq-linux epic convention).

Fix-plan steps 1 and 2 landed in 2e28291c.

Step 1: off Apple the ABI v1 host-services table is now built in Rust (crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_fft.rs) on rustfft, replacing the scalar radix-2 kernel. All the dgen_fft.h conventions are preserved (unscaled both directions, natural bin order, split-complex in place, true complex product in the MAC). Both directions are planned per log2_size at setup creation together with process_with_scratch scratch, so transforms allocate nothing. Because generated code caches one setup per call site in a static and the audiograph engine runs graph nodes on a worker pool, each setup owns a small CAS-claimed workspace pool and falls back to the portable C kernel when contended rather than blocking the audio thread. Apple keeps vDSP byte-for-byte.

Step 2: the complex multiply-accumulate moved to Rust with an AVX2+FMA specialisation behind is_x86_feature_detected!, rather than changing the C build flags.

Measured on the i5-8250U (Surface, x86_64 Linux) 2026-08-26, hot-cache, release, via the #[ignore]d benchmark test throughput_of_the_shipped_table_against_the_portable_kernel:
